# Overview

Does the choice of scoring method change the estimated structural path?
How much does accounting for stage-1 estimation uncertainty change its
standard error? This vignette addresses these questions with a small
simulation of a two-factor latent regression.

We compare 2S-PA using regression, Bartlett, and unweighted item-mean scores
with joint SEM. All 2S-PA analyses account for measurement error in the
scores. For each scoring method, we compare the default stage-2 sampling
SE with the additional delta-method correction requested by
`tspa(corrected_se = TRUE)`. See
[Corrected Standard Errors](corrected-se.html) for the scope of that correction.

Because the population path is known, we can evaluate bias and the
proportion of 95% confidence intervals containing the true value
(*coverage*). These results illustrate the chosen model and simulation
conditions; they are not a general ranking of scoring methods.

The design:

- **Model** — a two-factor path model (`ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3`,
  `dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4`, `dem60 ~ ind60`).
- **Replications** — `B = 200` datasets at each of two sample sizes, `n = 100` and
  `n = 200`.
- **Compared estimators** — for each of {regression, Bartlett, sum} scores, the 2S-PA
  path estimate with its naive SE and its corrected SE; and the joint-model path
  estimate with its SE.

# Data-generating model

Each dataset is drawn from a two-factor CFA with a single structural path, on the
unit-factor-variance scale:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\texttt{ind60} & \sim N(0, 1), \\
\texttt{dem60} & = \gamma^* \, \texttt{ind60} + \zeta, \qquad \zeta \sim N(0, 1 - (\gamma^*)^2),\ \ \zeta \perp \texttt{ind60},
\end{aligned}
$$

so `Var(ind60) = Var(dem60) = 1` and the factor correlation is $\gamma^* = 0.5$.
Indicators load on their own factor with errors independent of the factor:

```{r dgp, message = FALSE}
library(lavaan)
library(R2spa)
x <- readRDS("sim_scoring_se.RDS")
meta <- x$meta
cat(
  "gamma* (true std.all path) = ", meta$gamma_star, "\n",
  "ind60 loadings (x1,x2,x3)  = ", paste(round(meta$lam_ind, 2), collapse = ", "), "\n",
  "dem60 loadings (y1..y4)    = ", paste(round(meta$lam_dem, 2), collapse = ", "), "\n",
  "n = ", paste(meta$n, collapse = ", "), "  B = ", meta$B, "  seed = ", meta$seed, "\n",
  sep = ""
)
```

The true quantity of interest is the **standardized** (std.all) structural path, which
equals $\gamma^* = 0.5$ on this scale.

# Estimators compared

## Joint SEM

The joint SEM estimates the measurement parameters and structural path
simultaneously. The first loading of each factor is fixed to one
(marker-indicator identification). We use `standardizedSolution()` to
express the path in SD units, so it can be compared with the population
value of 0.5 and with the 2S-PA estimates.

An alternative identification, `std.lv = TRUE`, would also be valid.
For an endogenous factor in a structural model, however, that option fixes
its residual variance rather than its total variance. Comparing standardized
paths avoids confusing that scaling choice with the population coefficient.

## 2S-PA

For each scoring method `m` in {`"regression"`, `"Bartlett"`, `"mean"`}:

1. Stage 1 — fit the CFA (`std.lv = TRUE`, the usual scoring scale) and score it:
   `get_fs(fit, method = m, vfsLT = TRUE)`, to enable the corrected SE below.
2. Stage 2 — `tspa("dem60 ~ ind60", scores)`, reading `fsL`/`fsT` from the stage-1
   result. The naive SE is `vcov()` of that fit; the corrected SE additionally passes
   `corrected_se = TRUE` with the stage-1 `vfsLT`.
3. Read the path and its SE on the std.all scale via `standardizedSolution()`.

The score measurement parameters differ by scoring method:

- **Bartlett** scores have unit own-factor loadings and zero cross-loadings
  (identity `fsL`). Only score error variances/covariances need to be propagated
  (`which_free` = the free `fsT` positions).
- **Regression** scores have estimated score loadings as well as error
  variances/covariances.
- **Item-mean** scores use fixed item weights, but their score loadings
  still depend on the estimated item loadings. Their correction therefore
  includes both score loadings and error variances/covariances.

# Results

```{r summ, message = FALSE}
res <- x$res
gamma_star <- meta$gamma_star

summ <- function(g, se) {
  lo <- g - 1.96 * se; hi <- g + 1.96 * se
  c(bias = mean(g) - gamma_star, mc_sd = sd(g),
    mean_se = mean(se), calib = mean(se) / sd(g),
    coverage = mean(lo <= gamma_star & gamma_star <= hi))
}
cov95 <- function(g, se) mean((g - 1.96 * se) <= gamma_star &
                                  (g + 1.96 * se) >= gamma_star)
n_list <- meta$n
```

## Point estimates

The bias and Monte Carlo SD of the std.all path estimate, per method and sample size
(the corrected SE does not change the point estimate, so it is shown once per method):

```{r point-est}
pt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(n_list, function(n) {
  d <- res[res$n == n, ]
  data.frame(
    n = n,
    method = c("regression", "Bartlett", "item mean", "joint SEM"),
    bias = c(mean(d$est_reg) - gamma_star, mean(d$est_bar) - gamma_star,
             mean(d$est_sum) - gamma_star, mean(d$est_joint) - gamma_star),
    mc_sd = c(sd(d$est_reg), sd(d$est_bar), sd(d$est_sum), sd(d$est_joint)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
pt[, c("bias", "mc_sd")] <- round(pt[, c("bias", "mc_sd")], 4)
knitr::kable(pt, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Point estimates (std.all path). True value = 0.5.")
```

The estimated biases are small and the Monte Carlo SDs are similar in
these conditions. The three scoring methods give similar structural
estimates after accounting for their different score measurement properties.
This finding concerns the specified two-factor model, not all possible
measurement models or sample sizes.

## Standard errors

The mean reported SE, its calibration (mean SE / Monte Carlo SD), and the empirical
95% coverage, per method and SE treatment:

```{r se-table}
se_tbl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(n_list, function(n) {
  d <- res[res$n == n, ]
  data.frame(
    n = n,
    method = c("regression", "regression", "Bartlett", "Bartlett", "item mean", "item mean",
               "joint SEM"),
    se = c("naive", "corrected", "naive", "corrected", "naive", "corrected", "naive"),
    mean_se = c(mean(d$se_reg_naive), mean(d$se_reg_corr),
                mean(d$se_bar_naive), mean(d$se_bar_corr),
                mean(d$se_sum_naive), mean(d$se_sum_corr), mean(d$se_joint)),
    calib = c(mean(d$se_reg_naive) / sd(d$est_reg), mean(d$se_reg_corr) / sd(d$est_reg),
              mean(d$se_bar_naive) / sd(d$est_bar), mean(d$se_bar_corr) / sd(d$est_bar),
              mean(d$se_sum_naive) / sd(d$est_sum), mean(d$se_sum_corr) / sd(d$est_sum),
              mean(d$se_joint) / sd(d$est_joint)),
    coverage = c(summ(d$est_reg, d$se_reg_naive)["coverage"],
                 cov95(d$est_reg, d$se_reg_corr),
                 summ(d$est_bar, d$se_bar_naive)["coverage"],
                 cov95(d$est_bar, d$se_bar_corr),
                 summ(d$est_sum, d$se_sum_naive)["coverage"],
                 cov95(d$est_sum, d$se_sum_corr),
                 summ(d$est_joint, d$se_joint)["coverage"]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
se_tbl[, c("mean_se", "calib", "coverage")] <-
  round(se_tbl[, c("mean_se", "calib", "coverage")], 3)
knitr::kable(se_tbl, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Standard errors (std.all path). True value = 0.5; nominal coverage 0.95.")
```

# Discussion

- **Point estimates:** The 2S-PA estimates have small observed biases and
  precision similar to joint SEM in this study.
- **Default standard errors:** The default 2S-PA SEs are close to the joint
  SEM SEs. Their coverage is somewhat below 95% in several conditions.
- **Additional SE correction:** The correction has the largest effect for
  regression scores here, increasing coverage above 95%. Its effect on
  Bartlett and item-mean scoring is smaller. Increasing an SE can improve
  coverage when the default SE is too small, but can also produce conservative
  intervals.

The differences concern sampling uncertainty, not the measurement-error
correction of the path estimates: both SE versions use the same corrected
point estimate. With only 200 replications per condition, a coverage
estimate near 95% has a Monte Carlo SE of about 1.5 percentage points.
Small coverage differences should therefore be interpreted cautiously.

# Reproducibility

The per-replication table is cached in `sim_scoring_se.RDS` (this vignette's directory);
the code below regenerates it. It runs in a few minutes.

```{r sim-loop, eval = FALSE}
gamma_star <- 0.5
lam_ind <- c(0.80, 0.75, 0.85)   # ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
lam_dem <- c(0.75, 0.80, 0.70, 0.85)   # dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
cfa_model <- "ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3\ndem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4"
sem_model <- paste0(cfa_model, "\ndem60 ~ ind60")   # marker indicators, no std.lv

sim_one <- function(n) {
  ind <- rnorm(n)
  dem <- gamma_star * ind + rnorm(n, sd = sqrt(1 - gamma_star^2))
  data.frame(
    x1 = lam_ind[1] * ind + rnorm(n, sd = sqrt(1 - lam_ind[1]^2)),
    x2 = lam_ind[2] * ind + rnorm(n, sd = sqrt(1 - lam_ind[2]^2)),
    x3 = lam_ind[3] * ind + rnorm(n, sd = sqrt(1 - lam_ind[3]^2)),
    y1 = lam_dem[1] * dem + rnorm(n, sd = sqrt(1 - lam_dem[1]^2)),
    y2 = lam_dem[2] * dem + rnorm(n, sd = sqrt(1 - lam_dem[2]^2)),
    y3 = lam_dem[3] * dem + rnorm(n, sd = sqrt(1 - lam_dem[3]^2)),
    y4 = lam_dem[4] * dem + rnorm(n, sd = sqrt(1 - lam_dem[4]^2)))
}

stdall <- function(fit) {
  s <- standardizedSolution(fit, type = "std.all")
  i <- which(s$lhs == "dem60" & s$op == "~" & s$rhs == "ind60")
  c(est = s$est.std[i], se = s$se[i])
}
corr_fit <- function(fs) {
  v <- attr(fs, "vfsLT"); wf <- which(diag(v) > 1e-12)
  tspa("dem60 ~ ind60", fs, vfsLT = v[wf, wf], which_free = wf,
       corrected_se = TRUE)
}

run_rep <- function(n) {
  d   <- sim_one(n)
  cf  <- cfa(cfa_model, d, std.lv = TRUE)
  sem <- sem(sem_model, d)
  sr  <- get_fs(cf, method = "regression", vfsLT = TRUE)
  sb  <- get_fs(cf, method = "Bartlett",  vfsLT = TRUE)
   ss  <- get_fs(cf, method = "mean", vfsLT = TRUE)
  tr  <- tspa("dem60 ~ ind60", sr)
  tb  <- tspa("dem60 ~ ind60", sb)
  ts  <- tspa("dem60 ~ ind60", ss)
   trc <- corr_fit(sr); tbc <- corr_fit(sb); tsc <- corr_fit(ss)
  g <- stdall(sem); gr <- stdall(tr); gsc <- stdall(trc)
   gb <- stdall(tb); gscb <- stdall(tbc); gs <- stdall(ts); gscs <- stdall(tsc)
  c(est_reg = gr[["est"]], se_reg_naive = gr[["se"]], se_reg_corr = gsc[["se"]],
    est_bar = gb[["est"]], se_bar_naive = gb[["se"]], se_bar_corr = gscb[["se"]],
     est_sum = gs[["est"]], se_sum_naive = gs[["se"]], se_sum_corr = gscs[["se"]],
     est_joint = g[["est"]], se_joint = g[["se"]])
}

n_list <- c(100, 200); B <- 200
set.seed(20260830)
res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(n_list, function(n) {
  out <- as.data.frame(t(vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) run_rep(n), numeric(11))))
  out$n <- n; out$rep <- seq_len(B); out
}))
saveRDS(list(res = res, meta = list(gamma_star = gamma_star,
                                    lam_ind = lam_ind, lam_dem = lam_dem,
                                    n = n_list, B = B, seed = 20260830)),
        file = "sim_scoring_se.RDS")
```
